[Anthropic] Anthropic, PBC is an American artificial intelligence (AI) public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco, California. Its flagship product is Claude, a series of proprietary large language models (LLMs). In January 2021, with the goal of promoting AI safety, Anthropic was founded by former members of OpenAI, including siblings Daniela Amodei and Dario Amodei, who are president and CEO, respectively. The company is privately held but plans an initial public offering in November 2026. Valued at $965 billion in a May 2026 Series H capital raise, Anthropic is the world's most valuable AI pure play, rivaled by OpenAI. Anthropic develops the LLM Claude in four tiers: Fable, Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku. Claude is accessible via an online chatbot, an API, and Anthropic's agent harnesses: Claude Code, Cowork, Design, and Science. Its model class Claude Mythos, a less restricted version of Fable, is available only to approved US organizations with a cybersecurity and life sciences focus. Anthropic's Project Panama, internally described as an "effort to destructively scan all the books in the world", provides training data for Claude. Before Project Panama, Anthropic downloaded pirated books and was sued, settling in 2025 a copyright infringement lawsuit from authors for $1.5 billion. Anthropic conducts LLM research including on mechanistic interpretability, safety, alignment, and societal impact. Notable researchers working at Anthropic include Andrej Karpathy, John M. Jumper, Jan Leike, Chris Olah, Amanda Askell, and Levent Alpöge. Anthropic partners with cloud providers including Palantir. From 2024, Claude was used by the US Department of Defense (DoD) and the Intelligence Community. In 2026, Claude was used in the Iran war and the US intervention in Venezuela.
